messages:
Aisha: IncidentBot paged me for a runtime 5xx spike hitting /v1/generate in us-west ~5m ago. Errors ~18% over 1m. I'm starting a short handoff — I'm offline in ~35m so need coverage. Initial checks: retries are happening, failover to other regions partially triggered but sticky sessions keep traffic hitting the bad pool. IncidentBot details: https://incidents.internal/redwood/1840123456

IncidentBot: INCIDENT CREATED — INC-2026-452: runtime 5xx spike (service: runtime-service, region: prod-us-west). Autoscoped metrics attached. Pager: eng-oncall.

Tyler: I'm available, can take primary after ~20m. What's current mitigation and do you need me sooner?

Aisha: Plan so far: 1) disable session affinity for the /v1/generate route (temporary) 2) bump replica count for runtime-pool-3 in us-west 3) watch error rate and latency. Runbook I'm following: https://runbooks.internal/redwood/runtime-5xx (see "failover and scale" section). Executed disabling affinity now. If scaling doesn't improve in 10m escalate to infra.

Priya: If you want me on standby I can check host-level metrics and driver logs (possible GPU OOM). If it's node-level we should cordon/drain. I can also add an extra node to the pool.

Marco: FYI support — we have reports from a handful of paying customers seeing 502/timeout; no clear data corruption reports. Marco (CS): can you list affected customers so we can prioritize comms?

Marco (CS): A, B, C reported errors in the last 10m. Ticket numbers: #3872, #3875, #3880. Drafting a short status: "Investigating elevated errors in text generation (us-west). No customer data exposure detected. We will update within 30 minutes."

Jing: From a security POV I don't see obvious signatures of exploitation. Traffic profile looks distributed; no single malicious IP spike. If you see repeated auth/permission errors ping me.

Aisha: Quick routing note — currently incident bot pages only eng-oncall. For host-level escalation we should page eng-infra-oncall automatically when host OOMs or node-level errors appear. Tyler, can you file a tiny follow-up RFC for escalation policy after this?

Tyler: Yup I will. For the immediate handoff: I'll be primary after 20m (per Aisha). Priya is secondary (infra). Marco will own customer comms. Jing on security standby. Handoff checklist I'm inheriting: 
- confirm affinity is disabled and remained so
- check replica health for runtime-pool-3
- monitor error rate + 95th latency
- look at KV cache backpressure logs
I'll post status every 10m.

IncidentBot: Automated action: Disabled affinity on /v1/generate for routing group prod/us-west. Retries set to 3. Scaling request queued for runtime-pool-3 +2 replicas.

Priya: I pulled host metrics — node gpu-ovo-7 showed memory pressure and several OOM_kill events around the start of the spike. I'm cordoning and draining it now; starting a replacement node (node-template: gpu-v2). If the new node joins healthy we should see backend errors drop.

Aisha: Thanks. Also: if this looks like a resource exhaustion pattern in the near term we should consider a temporary quota throttle on heavier customers until we stabilize. Marco can coordinate messaging with CSM.

Marco (CS): Doing that. Draft updated: "We are prioritizing customers A and B for mitigation. If issues persist we'll divert traffic to other regions; no data loss expected. Next update in 20 minutes or upon resolution." :loudspeaker:

Jing: Security follow-up: correlation of client IPs shows distributed traffic across multiple ASNs, so not a single attacker or mistyped client. No elevated 401/403 patterns. I'll close the security watch unless new anomalies appear.

Priya: Drain finished, replacement node joined, pods rescheduled. Early signal: error rate down to ~4% (from 18%). Keeping an eye on latency.

Tyler: Taking over as primary now (Aisha handing off). Current state: error rate trending down, new node healthy, affinity still disabled. Keeping Priya as secondary. Marco continue with customer comms. Jing standby for security escalations only. I will keep 10m cadence updates.

Aisha: Handing off. Tyler primary, Priya secondary. I'll be reachable but stepping away. If error rate creeps above 5% for 15m escalate to full infra paging and consider rollback of any recent runtime-side changes. Runbook pointer again: https://runbooks.internal/redwood/runtime-5xx#handoff

Tyler: Update [+10m]: error rate steady ~3-5%. Latency within SLO. No further escalation required. Re-enable affinity only after 1 hour of stable metrics and quiescent sessions.

Marco (CS): Notifying affected accounts we've got improvements and are monitoring. CSMs looped.

IncidentBot: INCIDENT RESOLVED — INC-2026-452 closed by Tyler. Summary: node OOM -> draining + replacement + temporary disable affinity -> errors reduced. See postmortem plan: owners Tyler/Priya.

Tyler: Postmortem followups: 1) update escalation policy so infra is paged for node-level signals, 2) add a small autoscaler cooldown tweak to avoid repeated OOM cycles, 3) improve per-customer rate introspection in support UI. Filing tasks now.

Priya: Agree on followups. I'll attach driver logs and node timeline to the postmortem.

Aisha: Great handoff, thanks everyone. :raised_hands:
